context_requirements: Cells must be actively cycling with intact G2/M checkpoint signaling for the expected cell-cycle transcriptional response.
Functional p53 (TP53 wild-type) is required for robust CDKN1A/GADD45A induction; TP53-mutant lines may show weaker or absent p53-dependent arm.
Expression of CDC25 isoforms (A/B/C) is required for the inhibitor to engage its target; lines with low CDC25 expression may respond weakly.
RB-proficient cells are needed for sustained G1/S repression; RB-loss lines may show blunted CDKN1A-mediated arrest.
falsifiers: No decrease in CDC25A/B/C or cell-cycle genes (CCNA2, CCNB1, CDK1, CDC20) at 24 h in any line.
No induction of CDKN1A, GADD45A, or other p53 targets at 6 or 24 h in TP53-wild-type lines.
Cell-cycle gene changes indistinguishable from vehicle across all nine lines at both time points.
A response pattern dominated by generic stress (HSPA1A, HSPB1, DNAJB1) without cell-cycle gene suppression.

changes: Removed PLK1 from proximal_up and late_up: CDC25 inhibition causes G2/M arrest and PLK1 is a mitotic kinase whose transcription is cell-cycle regulated, so it should decrease, not increase.
Removed PLK1 from late_up for the same reason; it is not a p53/checkpoint-induced gene.
Kept CDKN1A, GADD45A, GADD45B, SFN, TP53BP2, DUSP4, DUSP6, FOS, JUN, EGR1, IER3, ATF5, TRIB3, SESN1 as up: these are consistent with checkpoint/p53/AP-1 stress responses to CDC25 inhibition.

Kept CCNA2, CCNB1, CCNB2, CDK1, CDC20, CDC45, MCM3, PCNA, TOP2A, AURKA, AURKB, BIRC5, KIF20A, KIF2C, NUSAP1 as down: CDC25 inhibition blocks CDK1 activation and causes G2/M arrest, reducing these cell-cycle genes.
No gene appears in both up and down lists at the same time point after removing PLK1 from up lists.
No generic proliferation or stress genes were present in the proximal lists beyond those already justified as direct checkpoint/p53 targets.
Line responses retained: A375, A549, HCC515, HT29, MCF7 moderate; HA1E, HEPG2, PC3, VCAP weak, consistent with TP53 status and cycling state.
Kinetics and magnitude retained: slow kinetics with weak 6 h and moderate 24 h effects is consistent with transcriptional consequences of CDC25 inhibition.
Evidence list left empty because no citations were provided to verify.
